clue.text: Mites in water ruined drink

indicators.note: ruined says the words before it are wrecked and put back together in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone finds tiny bugs in the water and declares the drink spoilt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruined' rearranges MITES IN WATER, all twelve letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweet martini is a cocktail of gin and sweet vermouth, so it is a drink.

clue.text: Joker to follow African flier

parts.note: a wag is a joker, a witty person
to tail someone is to follow them

explanation.surface: A clown sets off after a bird from Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: The African pied wagtail is a small bird found across Africa, so it is a flier there.

clue.text: They turn out to be winners after final whistle

indicators.note: after says the winners come behind the letter taken from whistle
final picks out the closing letter of the word whistle that follows it

parts.note: victors are winners

explanation.surface: The players who come out on top once the referee blows for full time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be' is a link; the winners come after the last letter of 'whistle'.
explanation.definitionFit: Evictors are those who throw tenants out of a property, that is who turn them out.

clue.text: Rome could be further

indicators.note: could be suggests the letters of Rome might become something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone muses that the Italian capital might be a longer trip.
explanation.definitionFit: Further and more both mean additional, as in a further or more question.

clue.text: Rose tries turning one into a restaurant

indicators.note: into says the letter for one goes inside the rearranged letters
turning says the letters of Rose tries are spun round into a new order

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A woman called Rose attempts to convert something into an eatery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' rearranges ROSE TRIES, and 'into' puts I (one) among those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotisserie is an eating place specialising in meat roasted on a spit, so a kind of restaurant.

clue.text: Silly Tina never takes part

indicators.note: takes part says only a portion of the words Tina never is wanted, a run inside them

explanation.surface: A girl called Tina never joins in, which seems foolish.
explanation.definitionFit: Inane means senseless or foolish, a synonym of silly.

clue.text: Live in in home a winner with Jack

parts.note: in at home means in, so in home stands for the word in

indicators.note: with here means having, so the winner holds the sailor inside it

parts.note: a hit is a success, a winner
a jack, or jack tar, is a sailor, abbreviated AB for able seaman

explanation.surface: A rambling description of life at home with a winner called Jack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a' is a link: 'a winner' is a hit. Jack is a sailor, a jack tar; 'with' means holding here.
explanation.definitionFit: To inhabit a place is to occupy or dwell there, to reside in it.

clue.text: One giving out money but about to refuse chemist

parts.note: C is short for circa, Latin for about
ash is refuse left after burning
a dispenser is a pharmacist who makes up prescriptions

explanation.surface: A machine that pays out cash is about to turn down a pharmacist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'refuse' looks like a verb but is the noun, waste. 'but' and 'to' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A cash dispenser is an automatic teller machine, which issues banknotes.

clue.text: Nuts on new engine ground by a British manufacturer?

parts.note: nuts means crazy, mad

indicators.note: new says the letters of engine are made afresh in a different order

parts.note: ground means land, earth

explanation.surface: Bolts and nuts on a brand-new engine are machined by a British firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nuts' looks like hardware but means MAD; 'ground' looks like machining but is LAND. 'new' rearranges ENGINE into EINENG; 'on' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods produced by a British maker carry the label saying they were produced in that country.

clue.text: More indignant, I rang poor Elizabeth

indicators.note: poor suggests I rang is badly formed and must be rearranged

parts.note: ER is Elizabeth Regina, the royal cipher of Queen Elizabeth

explanation.surface: Someone phoned unlucky Elizabeth, who became more cross.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poor' rearranges I RANG into ANGRI, and ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen's cipher.
explanation.definitionFit: Angrier is the comparative of angry, which means indignant or cross.

clue.text: The emergency service inserted a pipe for air

indicators.note: inserted says the emergency service goes into the word before it

parts.note: taken as written
the RAC, Royal Automobile Club, is a British roadside breakdown rescue service

explanation.surface: Rescue workers fitted a breathing tube.
explanation.walkthrough: The RAC is a British motoring club whose patrols rescue broken-down cars; 'inserted' puts it into the clue's own 'The'.
explanation.definitionFit: The trachea is the windpipe, carrying breath to the lungs.

clue.text: Man with craft centre

parts.note: a man is referred to as he
art is skill, craft

explanation.surface: A man stands with a craft display in the middle of town.
explanation.definitionFit: The heart of something is its core or middle.

clue.text: A "bless me when sick" col-leet

indicators.note: when sick says the letters of bless me are unwell, put into disorder

explanation.surface: Someone says bless me while ill, then gathers things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when sick' rearranges BLESS ME into SSEMBLE; the clue's 'col-leet' is a print slip for 'collect'.
explanation.definitionFit: To assemble people or things is to gather or bring them together.

clue.text: Drug misery hit man

parts.note: pain is suffering, misery
a hit man is a hired killer

explanation.surface: A contract killer is a wretched dealer in narcotics.
explanation.definitionFit: A painkiller is an analgesic medicine, a type of drug.

clue.text: Abused by doctor I left and went ahead without

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside says the going-ahead word wraps around the doctor word

parts.note: led means went in front, went ahead
to treat a patient is to doctor them

explanation.surface: A patient complains of mistreatment by a doctor, so walked out and carried on alone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, the went-ahead word wrapping the doctor word; 'by' and 'and' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill-treated means treated cruelly or badly, the same as mistreated.

clue.text: To knock out a daily paper takes time

indicators.note: takes means holds within, so the paper contains the letter for time

parts.note: The Sun is a British daily tabloid newspaper

explanation.surface: A tabloid takes its time to land a punch.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sun is a British daily tabloid; it takes T (time) inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To stun someone is to daze them into unconsciousness with a blow.

clue.text: One admits turning

parts.note: the thing that lets visitors in when someone twists it, the handle on an entrance

explanation.definitionFit: A doorknob is the round handle you rotate to open a door and let people in.

clue.text: Having very good piano backstage, sing

parts.note: pi is slang for pious, very good
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly
the back of the word stage is its last letter E

explanation.surface: A virtuous pianist waits in the wings, ready to perform a song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backstage' is read as the back of 'stage', its last letter. 'Having' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To pipe is to sing or play in a high, shrill voice, as birds do.

clue.text: Cautious pair tuned motors

indicators.note: motors means moves fast, so the letters of tuned are moved into a new order

explanation.surface: A careful couple who have had their cars tuned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'motors' looks like cars but is a verb, rearranging TUNED into UDENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Prudent means careful and wise, showing caution.

clue.text: Top poem among articles from Australia?

indicators.note: among says the top and the poem sit between the articles

parts.note: an is the indefinite article, taken twice
a tip is the top or point of something
an ode is a lyric poem

explanation.surface: A leading verse sits among some items said to come from Down Under.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top' looks like an adjective for the poem but is a noun of its own. The question mark flags a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: The Antipodes are Australia and New Zealand, so an Antipodean comes from there, among other places.

clue.text: During broadcast speaker raised Italian banker's shops

indicators.note: during says the Italian banker comes within the turned-up words
raised, in a down clue, says the words broadcast speaker are read upwards

parts.note: to air a programme is to broadcast it
the speaker of a sentence refers to themself as me
a banker is a river, something with banks; the Po is Italy's longest river

explanation.surface: A loudspeaker lifted during an Italian financier's trip round the stores.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns AIR + ME into EMRIA; 'During' puts PO inside. 'banker' is crossword shorthand for a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Emporia, plural of emporium, are large stores or marketplaces.

clue.text: No truce arranged I admitted being nervous

indicators.note: admitted says the letters let the I in, holding it inside
arranged says the letters of No truce are set out in a different order

explanation.surface: Without a ceasefire deal, one confessed to being on edge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' rearranges NO TRUCE and 'admitted' takes in I. 'being' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Neurotic means anxious and highly strung, overly nervous.

clue.text: Egg-shaped tank in empty outhouse

indicators.note: in says the tank goes inside the shell of the outhouse
empty says the outhouse loses everything but its first and last letters

parts.note: a vat is a large tank for liquids

explanation.surface: An oval tank stands in a disused shed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty' leaves O and E, the first and last letters of 'outhouse'; VAT goes between.
explanation.definitionFit: Ovate describes an oval shape like that of an egg.

clue.text: Drive back before the Spanish salesman

indicators.note: before says the salesman comes ahead of the Spanish word

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: Pushing away a travelling salesman before the Spanish arrive.
explanation.definitionFit: To repel attackers is to repulse them, forcing them to retreat.

clue.text: Woman a man naturally keeps hidden!

indicators.note: keeps hidden says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A man instinctively conceals a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Anna is a girl's name, so it stands for a female person.

clue.text: Look over organ before social function

indicators.note: before says the organ comes ahead of the social function

parts.note: the eye is the organ of sight
a ball is a formal dance, a social function

explanation.surface: Inspecting an organ before going to a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: To eyeball something is to stare at it or inspect it closely.

clue.text: No pressing work to be done?

definitions.text: No pressing work to be done?

parts.words: No pressing work to be done?
parts.note: pressing sounds urgent but means smoothing clothes, which some fabrics never need

explanation.definitionFit: Non-iron fabric does not need ironing after washing, so it needs no pressing.

clue.text: Stars wanting a breather get replacement

indicators.note: replacement says the letters of a breather get are placed again in a new order

explanation.surface: Sports stars are tired and want a rest, so get a substitute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replacement' rearranges A BREATHER GET; 'wanting' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Great Bear, Ursa Major, is a constellation, a group of stars.
